exposure: Delayed postpartum IUD insertion at an outpatient visit
intended delayed insertion at an outpatient postpartum visit (delayed postpartum placement)
cohort: Theoretical cohort of 2,500,000 women intending to receive a postplacental IUD after vaginal birth, 1,250,000 women intending to receive a postplacental IUD after cesarean birth, and 2,500,000 women intending to receive a delayed postpartum IUD
finding: The decision analysis model indicated that intended postplacental IUD insertion resulted in a lower 1-year probability of pregnancy compared to intended delayed postpartum IUD insertion, after accounting for factors affecting successful IUD placement and retention.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was a factor in the decision analysis model comparing intended postplacental IUD insertion with intended delayed postpartum placement, finding different one-year probabilities of pregnancy for each mode.
